Access-Control-Allow-Headers.description: The request headers a client may send.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin.description: The request's Origin, only when it matches the configured allow-list (scheme and host ignoring case, port exactly once the scheme's default port, 443 for https and 80 for http, is dropped on both sides); never *.

Access-Control-Expose-Headers.description: The response headers a browser at an allowed origin may read: the back-off of 503 busy and the challenge of 401 unauthorized.

Access-Control-Max-Age.description: Seconds a preflight may be cached.

Vary.description: Origin, on every response while the server is configured with an allow-list of CORS origins, whatever the request's Origin.

BadRequest.description: The body, the inventory, the target list or a region is invalid. Codes: invalid_request, invalid_inventory, invalid_targets, invalid_region.

Busy.description: The concurrency cap is reached; retry later. Codes: busy.

Internal.description: An internal error; the message is always internal error. Codes: internal.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path does not allow this method. Codes: method_not_allowed.

MisdirectedRequest.description: The server is configured with an allow-list of hosts and the request's Host is not in it, compared ignoring case (an entry without a port matches any port). Checked before anything else; /healthz and /readyz are exempt. Codes: misdirected_request.

NotAcceptable.description: No representation the Accept header allows. Codes: not_acceptable.

NotFound.description: No route has this path. Codes: not_found.

NotReady.description: The readiness check failed. Codes: not_ready.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The body is over the cap. Codes: payload_too_large.

Unauthorized.description: A token is configured and the request does not carry it. Codes: unauthorized.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The body is not application/json, or has a charset other than utf-8. Codes: unsupported_media_type.

bearerAuth.description: Optional. When the server is configured with a token (an RFC 6750 token68), every /v1/ request must send Authorization: Bearer <token>, else 401 unauthorized with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, checked before the body is read. /healthz and /readyz never require it.

info.description: The HTTP API of shift2eu-server (PRD #103, docs/adr/0019). It takes inventory documents (docs/adr/0006) and answers with the JSON report (docs/adr/0018) or the Markdown report. It is stateless: nothing from a request is stored or logged. TLS and users belong to a reverse proxy. Every response, errors included, sets Cache-Control: no-store and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Every error has the shape of the Error schema. Two errors belong to no operation: a path no route has is 404 not_found (components.responses.NotFound), and a method a path does not declare is 405 method_not_allowed with an Allow header (components.responses.MethodNotAllowed). When the server is configured with an allow-list of hosts, a request whose Host is not in it is 421 misdirected_request (components.responses.MisdirectedRequest) on every path but /healthz and /readyz, before any other check, a 404 included. When the server is configured with an allow-list of CORS origins, every response carries Vary: Origin, and a response to an allowed Origin on a /v1/ path carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin with that origin and Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Retry-After, WWW-Authenticate. Within /v1/, adding a route, a response key, a header or an error code is not breaking; a breaking change is a /v2/ route.

get.summary: Readiness: 200 once every target's catalog has loaded, else 503.

options.description: Only when the server is configured with an allow-list of origins and the request's Origin is in it: 204 with the CORS headers. Any other OPTIONS request, including one from an origin not in the list, is 405. Never requires the token. A Host outside the configured allow-list of hosts is 421, before the preflight is answered.

post.description: One target answers with an assessment document; several, or ["all"], with a comparison document, in sorted key order. The JSON body is byte for byte what `shift2eu assess --format json` prints for the same inventory and targets, with the inventory named inventory.json. With Accept text/markdown (or text/*) the answer is the Markdown report, byte for byte the CLI's. No Accept, */*, application/* or application/json gives JSON; a range with q=0 is excluded, and one whose q is not a number in [0, 1] is skipped; nothing acceptable is 406. At most a configured number of assessments run at once; over it the request is refused at once with 503 busy.

requestBody.description: Content-Type must be application/json, else 415; a charset parameter other than utf-8 (compared ignoring case) is 415 too, as the body is decoded as UTF-8 only. The body is capped at the inventory reader's cap plus 64 KiB (413 over it), and decoded strictly: an unknown key, a repeated key (also ignoring case), a wrong type, null, invalid UTF-8 or trailing data is 400 invalid_request.

schema.description: The Markdown report, as text/markdown; charset=utf-8.

200.description: The report. The JSON report is schemaVersion 2 (docs/adr/0018, docs/adr/0030); a client reads schemaVersion to know which version it holds.
